paragraphs.text: Idiopathic torsion dystonia is a neurologic disorder characterized by sustained muscle contractions that appear as twisting movements of the limbs, trunk, and/or neck, which can progress to abnormal postures (Kramer et al., 1990; Kwiatkowski et al., 1991). The DYT1 form begins early, usually in childhood, and typically starts in a limb (Bressman et al., 1994; Ozelius et al., 1997). It is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner with reduced penetrance of 30 to 40% (Ozelius et al., 1997), and it is particularly frequent among Ashkenazi Jews (Kramer et al., 1990).

However, the authors observed one example of a benign, adult-onset dominant form associated with tremor.

paragraphs.text: Bressman et al. (1994) studied 174 Ashkenazi Jewish individuals with idiopathic torsion dystonia. Using chromosome 9q34 markers, they classified 90 as carriers of the DYT1-associated haplotype, 70 as noncarriers, and 14 as ambiguous. Mean age at onset was 12.5 +/- 8.2 years in carriers and 36.5 +/- 16.4 years in noncarriers. In 94% of carriers, symptoms began in a limb, with arm and leg affected equally often. Onset was rarely in the neck (3.3%) or larynx (2.2%). In contrast, 79% of noncarriers had onset in the neck, larynx, or other cranial muscles, 21% had onset in the arms, and none had onset in the legs. Limb onset, leg involvement during the course of the disease, and age at onset together distinguished carriers from noncarriers with 90% accuracy.

paragraphs.text: Heiman et al. (2004) gave a standardized psychiatric interview to members of families with a DYT1 mutation. Compared with 65 noncarriers, the risk of recurrent major depressive disorder was increased both in 60 nonmanifesting carriers (relative risk 4.95, CI 1.72 to 14.29) and in 96 manifesting carriers (relative risk 3.62, CI 1.00 to 10.53). Carriers also had an earlier age at onset of recurrent major depression. The severity of motor signs was not associated with the likelihood of recurrent depression, and carriers did not have an increased risk of single major depression or bipolar disorder. The authors suggested that early-onset recurrent depression is a clinical expression of the DYT1 mutation.

paragraphs.text: Calakos et al. (2010) studied a man in his fifth decade who had had involuntary jaw movements and grimacing for 3 years, consistent with oromandibular dystonia. He also had bipolar disorder treated with lithium and remote exposure to dopamine receptor-blocking agents, and his family history included tremor and depression but no dystonia. Sequencing of TOR1A identified a c.613T-A change in exon 3, resulting in a phe205-to-ile (F205I) substitution at a highly conserved residue in the AAA-ATPase domain. The variant was not found in 800 population controls. In transfected BHK cells, the F205I mutant produced inclusions in 44% of cells, compared with 10% for wildtype and 79% for the delta-E mutant. However, F205I inclusions colocalized mainly with the endoplasmic reticulum marker KDEL rather than with the nuclear envelope marker lamin B1. The authors raised the possibility that the variant may contribute to late-onset focal dystonia.

checks.claim: TorsinA residue phe205 is highly conserved and located in the AAA-ATPase domain.
checks.evidence_quote: The phenylalanine at position 205 is highly conserved across species and is part of a highly conserved beta strand motif in the AAA domain (Figure 1B).

checks.claim: The TOR1A F205I variant was not found in 800 population controls.
checks.evidence_quote: This variant was not identified in 800 anonymized population controls (1600 chromosomes).

checks.claim: In transfected BHK cells, the TOR1A F205I mutant produced inclusions in 44% of cells.
checks.evidence_quote: F205I-TOR1A-EGFP frequently produced inclusions in transfected cells (44% F205I vs. 10% wildtype; p<0.05)

checks.claim: In transfected BHK cells, wildtype TOR1A produced inclusions in 10% of cells.
checks.evidence_quote: expression of wildtype TOR1A-EGFP only rarely resulted in cells with detectable inclusion bodies (10%) (Figure 2A)

checks.claim: In transfected BHK cells, the TOR1A delta-E mutant produced inclusions in 79% of cells.
checks.evidence_quote: expression of ΔE-TOR1A-EGFP frequently produced inclusion bodies in transfected cells (79% of transfected cells)

checks.claim: TOR1A F205I inclusions colocalized mainly with the endoplasmic reticulum marker KDEL rather than with the nuclear envelope marker lamin B1.
checks.evidence_quote: F205I mutant TOR1A, in contrast to the pronounced colocalization of ΔE TOR1A with nuclear envelope markers, preferentially colocalized with the ER marker, KDEL (96%, n=67 cells) relative to Lamin B1 (19%, n=41 cells).

checks.claim: Calakos et al. (2010) raised the possibility that the TOR1A F205I variant may contribute to late-onset focal dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: Together, these observations raise the possibility that the c.613T>A, p.F205I variant of TOR1A may contribute to the presentation of late-onset, focal dystonia by altering the normal activity of TOR1A.
